children: The main U.S. stock indexes are lower early Wednesday as a surge in oil prices fuels concerns about deepening tensions in the Middle East. Brent crude futures climbed above $100 per barrel for the first time since July.
Nearly all S&P 500 sectors are now in negative territory, with consumer discretionary
, both down 1%, leading the declines. Energy
, up 1%, is the only sector in the green. The energy sector is on pace for a record closing high.
Beneath the surface, gold and silver miners (.XAU) are among the market's better performers.
Investors are also keeping an eye on Apple

, which is set to hold a launch event expected to feature the latest versions of its flagship products. The event marks the company's first major product unveiling since John Ternus succeeded Tim Cook as CEO. Apple shares are modestly lower on the day.
Here is a snapshot of where markets stood around 10:15 a.m. EDT.
Main US indexes red; Dow off most, down ~0.8%
Consumer Discretionary is weakest S&P 500 sector; energy is sole gainer
Dollar dips; bitcoin gains; gold up >1%; US crude gains >3%
US 10-year Treasury yield edges up to ~4.81%
